thread:
Zoe Park: kicking off ravenna-embed-v1 onboarding. did a quick FP16 -> int8 smoke and seeing recall@1 drop and odd tiny clusters. posting minimal output below for triage. :eyes:

Zoe Park: command i ran:
```
python infra/evals/recall.py --model=ravenna-embed-v1 --quant=int8 --dataset=holdout_seed --k=10
```

Zoe Park: quick metrics (FP16 -> INT8):
``
recall@1: 0.714 -> 0.655
recall@5: 0.882 -> 0.857
silhouette: 0.32 -> 0.18
median_l2_norm: 8.2 -> 0.09
```

Samir Patel: whoa median L2 norm dropping to 0.09 screams quant scale issue. can you dump per-vector norms and quant scales? might be zeroed scales in per-channel quant?

Zoe Park: yeah grabbing norms now, will paste a tiny sample. tagging @kai in case it's an encoder export bug.

Kai Nguyen: grabbing the sample from Zoe's run, here's head of norms.csv (col: id,l2_norm,quant_scale):
``
1001,7.9,0.125
1002,8.1,0.128
1003,0.03,0.0000
1004,0.02,0.0000
1005,7.7,0.122
1006,0.01,0.0000
```

Kai Nguyen: looks like some rows have quant_scale==0.0000 which would collapse values to ~0 after dequant. that explains tiny clusters (embeddings collapsing to near-zero vectors).

Maria Lopez: could be edge-case when partition has no variance and our scale computation did clamping to zero. check clamping logic in quantizer (min_scale epsilon). also try per-tensor quant as a quick comparison.

Samir Patel: can we repro on CPU (no kernels) to rule out a runtime/AVX bug? run `python infra/evals/recall.py --model=ravenna-embed-v1 --quant=int8 --force-cpu` and also run a small script to assert scale>1e-6 for all channels.

Zoe Park: running CPU now, will attach full norm histogram.

Zoe Park: histogram summary (counts):
``
norm < 0.1: 312
0.1 <= norm < 1: 120
norm >= 1: 3568
```

Zoe Park: so ~8% are collapsed. that's enough to knock down recall@1 in tail-heavy holdout.

Kai Nguyen: probable root cause: our export step for some shards uses int16 accumulator path that writes scales but forgets to set fallback epsilon when max==min. PR incoming from me to set scale = max(eps, computed_scale).

Samir Patel: +1 to Kai. also add a quick unit test: generate constant vectors and assert quant_scale >= eps and dequant roundtrip preserves norm within tolerance.

Maria Lopez: for immediate unblock, do a canary: re-run recall with a filter that excludes collapsed vectors and measure delta. helps quantify how much user-visible regression is from those rows vs broader quantization error.

Zoe Park: did that: filtered-run (drop norm < 0.1) gave recall@1: 0.703 (vs 0.714 FP16). so most of the regression is from collapsed vectors, not global quant shift.

eval-bot: Experiment summary (run: https://redwood-runs/ui/1771239999): compared ravenna-embed-v1 FP16 vs INT8. Observed regression on holdout_seed. Notable: ~8% collapsed vectors (scale==0). Recommend fixing scale clamping, add unit test, re-run full holdout, and run small production-like client test.

Samir Patel: i'll own the follow-up test matrix (per-tensor vs per-channel; clamp eps values 1e-6/1e-4/1e-2; CPU vs GPU). will log experiments under /experiments/ravenna/quantization/1771239999.

Kai Nguyen: pushed quick fix branch to set min_scale=1e-4 and a unit test. starting internal CI run now.

Zoe Park: thanks. once CI passes i'll re-run the full recall and clustering viz (t-SNE) and share images. also will open a short postmortem note describing the export corner case for onboarding docs.

Maria Lopez: also add an eval that measures recall@1 for short queries (len<=8) since that's where we saw worst drops in previous models.

Zoe Park: noted. assigning follow-ups: @Samir for experiments, @Kai for export bug fix/PR, @Maria for short-query eval addition. I'll re-run and report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
